test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What causes the cam lobes to make a ticking or tapping noise in the engine, especially at idle, and is often rhythmic and varies in intensity?

options.text: When the cam lobe is subjected to heavy load.
When there is insufficient lubrication in the cam lobe.
When the cam lobe is hot.
When the cam lobe wears out.

solution:
The correct answer is __When the cam lobe wears out.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cam lobe wear__ is a common reason for ticking or tapping noise in the engine.
 
• This wear can result from prolonged usage or insufficient lubrication.
 
• The noise is often rhythmic and can vary in intensity depending on the engine's condition.
 
• It is more noticeable at idle when the engine speed is low.
 
• If left unchecked, it can lead to serious engine damage.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Insufficient Lubrication:**

 
 
• Low oil levels or poor-quality oil can lead to inadequate lubrication of the cam lobe.
 
• This can accelerate wear and increase noise in the engine.
 
 
 
• **Heavy Load on Cam Lobe:**
 
 
• Excessive load can strain the cam lobe, but it is not a primary cause of ticking noise.
 
• Regular maintenance can help mitigate such issues.
 
 
 
• **Overheating:**
 
 
• When the engine overheats, it may cause minor noise, but it is usually not rhythmic or tapping.
 
• Proper cooling system maintenance helps avoid overheating-related issues.
